explanation: Fires on the function word (preposition/determiner such as 'as', 'by', 'with', 'in', 'on', 'every', 'all', 'the') right after a verb or phrase that sets up a comparison or shared application: 'treated in the same way as', 'example set by', 'as with all', 'add this node to every', 'worked on another device'. The 'same/similar/as with' context is the key cue; content words in the same frame are weaker, and ordinary prepositions without a comparison frame give little.

Fires on mid-word or word-completing subword tokens in a wide range of contexts: 'Message' in '-----Original Message-----', fragments of names and technical terms ('aspir|in', 'S|GB|D', 'Kaisersl|aut|ern', 'trache|al'), non-English word pieces (Greek, Japanese, Turkish, Russian), plus a few 'of' tokens and 'Christ'. No shared meaning is visible beyond being a highly predictable continuation token.

Fires on an inner subword piece of a rare proper name or technical word that is split into several tokens: surnames and place names ('B|ous|man', 'Th|ic|ke', 'H|ous|ley', ' Vander', 'Ras Al| Kh|air', 'Jamaat ul|-M|ujahideen'), taxonomic and chemical names ('Ph|yt|olacca', 'im|id|acloprid'). Common whole words give little activation.

Fires on the determiner or possessive ('the', 'a', 'your', 'their') right after a motion or location preposition/verb ('at', 'to', 'from', 'contact', 'tour') when the next words name a specific venue, organization or place (the Feral Cat Coalition, a party, the hospital, your local store). Strongest when someone goes to, visits or contacts a place; determiners in other roles are weak.

Fires in biomedical and materials-science abstract prose on the token that starts the object of a verb or relation, the thing being affected or studied (e.g. 'onset[[ of]] mastitis', 'inhibits[[ growth]]', 'essential for[[ normal]]', 'effects on[[ oste]]ogenic', 'lower[[ the]] quality'). It is about health or biological effects and outcomes; similar phrasing outside science or health text is weaker.

Fires on the word naming the substance in drug/substance-use contexts: 'drug', 'substance', 'Alcohol', 'opiate', 'marijuana', 'smoking', usually before 'abuse', 'use', 'trafficking' or 'tests'. Weaker on related health-behaviour words (medication adherence, contraceptive, adolescent).

Fires on subword pieces inside non-English or formal multi-token names and words, especially German/Spanish/Italian institution names ('Max-Planck-Institut[[ für]]', 'Instituto Nacional[[ del]]', 'Mathematik[[ und]]') and fragments of capitalized or foreign words split across tokens ('SUP|RE|ME', 'THIR|TE|ENTH', 'front|ot|emporal', Finnish/Swedish/Czech pieces). Plain English words give weak responses.

Mixed. Fires on chemical and drug name fragments ('gl|ut|am', 'glut|aryl', 'lact|ate', 'par|acet|amol', 'z|ot|epine'), on 'Tu' in Tuareg/Tuilagi, on license boilerplate ('CONTRIBUTORS BE LIABLE', 'DIRECT,'), on digits in IDs, and on words in biographical text ('student at', 'attended', 'studying'). No single shared feature.

Fires on the preposition, comma or 'the' that links a place to the larger region containing it in gazetteer-style descriptions ('nine miles east[[ of]]', 'capital city[[ of]]', 'administrative district[[ of]]', 'Miri Division[[,]] Sarawak', 'in[[ the]] Swiss canton'). Weaker on similar linking tokens ('of', 'from', 'in') in other descriptive text.

Fires on tokens in the header and boilerplate of US court opinions: 'court' in 'circuit court'/'court below', 'Appeal'/'Appe|al' from, 'MEM|OR|ANDUM', 'OPINION', 'Order', 'Case', and the whitespace runs in docket captions. Weaker on party labels ('Plaintiff') and in other legal or license boilerplate.

Fires on the surname of a person's full name, mostly on a later subword piece of a split surname ('Fryk|man', 'Sw|enson', 'Ferr|aro', 'McG|owan') or a whole surname token after a first name ('Mark Taylor', 'Max Klein', 'Joe Ellis'). Most common in news bylines, quotes and case captions. First names and non-name words do not fire.

Fires in physics and biology abstract prose on the function word or modifier that comes right after a technical noun or method and starts the next technical phrase ('projector[[ augmented]] wave', 'techniques[[ including]]', 'nanostructures[[ using]]', 'based[[ on]]', 'studied[[ using]]', 'ground state of[[ the]]'). It is a scientific methods-description register; ordinary prose gives little.

Fires on the first subword piece of a word that is split into several tokens, often a capitalized name or a non-English word ('[[ p]]one', '[[bec]]ome', 'Asco[[chy]]ta', '[[ Gr]]ays', '[[ Mir]]amar', 'TO BE[[ P]]UBLISHED', 'Motion[[ Rel]]ating'). Fires most when the opening fragment is short and the rest of the word follows. Whole common words do not fire.

Mixed. Fires on 'by', 'for' or 'using' after a measurement verb in scientific methods ('as assessed[[ by]]', 'measured[[ by]]', 'controlling[[ for]]', 'detected[[ using]]'), on subword or identifier pieces in code ('Typed[[Array]]', 'while[[(true]]', ': IS'), and on assorted nouns and suffixes ('miniatur[[ization]]', 'centre', 'Oxygen'). Only the measurement-method part is coherent.

Mixed. Fires on the last token of predictable multi-token phrases or words in many settings: list items (state codes 'IA'), boilerplate ('materials[[ provided]] with', 'GNU[[ Lesser]]', 'minifies[[ for]] production'), word completions ('imp[[et]]igo', 'KitchenA[[id]]', 'diast[[olic]]', 'oc[[ular]]') and collocations ('learning style', 'burger with fries'). No clear shared topic.

Fires on tokens in informal, conversational or narrative first-person text, especially the pronoun 'I' at the start of a quoted line or clause ('"I do not understand"', 'When I saw this, I thought'), and parts of casual idioms ('at the last second', 'can't wait', 'on the fence', 'came across', 'jump on the scene'). Formal or technical text gives little.

Mixed. Fires most on a zero inside long runs of zeros ('0000[[0]]0000'), and moderately on assorted tokens: LaTeX backslashes, spaces before numbers, subword pieces of German or foreign words ('Re|zipienten'), and SQL or code punctuation. No coherent theme beyond the zero runs.

Fires on acronym or abbreviation pieces and short capitalized codes inside proper names of organizations and products ('LE', 'CR', 'LLC', 'MAG', 'SEMA', 'MKE', 'NIGMS'), and on 'of' in 'University of X'. Strongest inside institution or product names; ordinary words give weak responses.

Fires on the token right after a noun-phrase head or determiner that starts an evaluative or descriptive modifier in expository prose ('a simple[[,]] specific', 'a simple[[ and]] noninvasive', 'one of the[[ leading]] causes', 'the[[ largest]]', 'his[[ many]] contributions', 'relatively infrequent[[ but]]'). Often adjective coordination or superlatives inside a definitional sentence. The pattern is loose.

Mixed. Fires on 'removed' in 'has been removed by mistake', the transpose prime in matrix formulas, digits in hashes, a Romanian word piece, and objects or complements of verbs ('without[[ restriction]]', 'break[[ something]]', 'are[[ crossed]]', 'pieces of paper[[ left]]'). No common thread.

Mixed. Fires on numbers and math tokens (score digits '5 runs', '2-2', '6-1', citation periods 'N.E.2d', '$x,y,z>0$', the 'g' in physics), and also on subword pieces in product or technical names ('Mash|able', 'Play|Mem|ories', 'electrom|y|ographic', 'Non-v|olatile'). Loosely tied to numeric or technical continuations.
